jobs.title: Associate, Private Climate Investing
jobs.description:
About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated and results-driven Associate to join our Private Climate Investing Team. The Climate Innovation Fund (“CIF”) is a growth stage fund investing in companies developing solutions that help mitigate and/or adapt to climate change, typically at the Series B-D stage. The investment strategy spans a broad set of sectors including energy, buildings, smart cities, industrial efficiency/automation, transportation and mobility, and food and agriculture, typically with asset-light tech-enabled solutions involving software, software-enabled hardware, and data/AI. 

The Associate will be involved in all aspects of the deal process and will work directly with our senior investment team to assist in the sourcing, diligence, and management of portfolio companies. The ideal candidate will be a self-directed, hard-working team player who is passionate about both private investing and climate.  This is a great opportunity for someone looking to join an experienced team and gain the foundations of venture investing and establish a career in VC with potential to progress in Wellington’s Private Investing platform.
 

ESSENTIAL SKILLS
The following essential skills are required for the role:

  • Analytical acumen, modeling, research –The ideal candidate will have strong financial modeling skills and demonstrated analytical capabilities and an eagerness to apply their expertise in support of CIF. The ability to synthesize disparate information during the diligence process, identify the most important elements, and translate findings into clear and concise materials is required. Proven expertise in market mapping and desktop research gained through prior professional experience.

  • Superior collaboration and influencing skills – The Associate will be a self-directed, hard-working team player, who contributes to the investment efforts of the CIF Investing team. The successful candidate will enjoy contributing to a highly collaborative investment environment and will build strong trusting relationships internally with colleagues across the Private Investing, Investment Research and Climate Research teams, as well as externally with portfolio companies and co-investors. 

  • Agility and flexibility – The Associate should enjoy working in a fast-paced environment and will need the ability to move seamlessly across workstreams, managing multiple projects and diligence streams simultaneously. 

  • Relationship building – Interest and desire to actively engage in the climate tech startup ecosystem, including networking with strategic contacts, attending industry events and conferences, building a rapport with founders, potential co-investors and engaging with leadership from CIF portfolio companies. 

  • Excellent communication skills – The ability to clearly communicate through verbal and written materials is critical when interacting with management teams, collaborating with internal and external partners, and drafting investment memos and other documents.  

  • Passion – The Associate will have an interest and curiosity for climate change impacts, as well as in emerging technologies and the application of technology to address global challenges. 

RESPONSIBILITIES
Responsibilities for this position will include the following:

  • Assisting with outbound market research and company mapping activities

  • Performing due diligence on prospective portfolio companies

  • Building and maintaining company financial models and other analysis on current and prospective investments

  • Drafting investment memos and participating in investment committee discussions 

  • Attending target company management meetings and relevant industry conferences 

  • Assist with quarterly and annual reporting needs for Limited Partners

  • Completing complex analytical projects under tight time constraints

OTHER QUALIFICATIONS
Additional qualifications and individual characteristics include:

  • Two to four years of prior experience preferably in investment banking, consulting, or venture capital; strong applicants with other relevant experience (e.g., investment management in public markets) will also be considered

  • Strong academic credentials and track record: an undergraduate degree is required 

  • Strong collaborative nature, including the ability to respectfully discuss and debate the merits and risks of potential investments with colleagues

  • Ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate market, industry, and company research, summarize large data sets, and identify patterns that enhance underwriting and monitoring workflows

  • Ability to organize, manage, and prioritize time well

  • Ability to work independently and make decisions in the face of uncertainty

  • Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving ability

  • Sound judgment, strong work ethic and highest personal and professional integrity

  • A growth mindset with the ability to receive and act on constructive feedback

  • A high degree of intellectual curiosity

  • Strong attention to detail 

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications?  That’s ok. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply and welcome a chance to review your background. We are dedicated to building and maintaining a diversified workforce and considering a broad array of candidates with a variety of skill, workplace experiences, and backgrounds.

As an equal opportunity employer, Wellington Management ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, creed, national origin, age, ancestry, disability (physical or mental), medical condition, citizenship, marital status, pregnancy, veteran or military status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you are a candidate with a disability, or are assisting a candidate with a disability, and require an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please email us at GMWTalentOperations@wellington.com.

At Wellington Management, our approach to compensation is designed to help us attract, inspire and retain the best talent in our industry. We strive to pay employees fairly and competitively across all levels and roles. Our approach to compensation considers all aspects of total compensation; all employees are eligible to receive salary, variable compensation, and benefits. The base salary range for this position is:

USD 90,000 - 180,000

This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered when making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; role; skills and experience; certifications; and education. This range is an estimate, and further details on salary and total compensation aspects will be shared with candidates during the recruitment process.

Base salary is only one component of Wellington’s total compensation approach. Other rewards may include a discretionary Corporate Bonus and/ or Incentives, if eligible. In addition, we offer a comprehensive and high value benefit package to meet the unique needs of our employees and their families, and we are committed to fostering a flexible work environment that enables employees to thrive personally and professionally.  Examples of our benefits include retirement plan, health and wellbeing, dental, vision, and pharmacy coverage, health savings account, flexible spending accounts and commuter program, employee assistance program, life and disability insurance, adoption assistance, back-up childcare, tuition/CFAreimbursement and paid time off (leave of absence, paid holidays, volunteer, sick and vacation time)

We believe that in person interactions inspire and energize our community and are essential to our culture. In support of this commitment, our employees work from our offices 4 days a week with flexibility to work remotely 1 day a week. We believe that this approach ultimately supports our mission to deliver investment excellence to our clients and their beneficiaries over the long term.

jobs.description:
Position Description

We are looking for an experienced FX/Rates Strategist to join our Economics & FICCs team. As a FX/Rates Strategist, you will be responsible for conducting in-depth analysis of FX and interest rate markets in Asia, factoring in the context of core global FX/rates markets. Your insights and recommendations will play a crucial role in supporting our clients' investment and hedging strategies. This position requires expertise in both currency and interest rate markets, as well as a deep understanding of the regulatory landscape, policy architecture, and market instruments in Asian markets. The role is based in in Singapore or Hong Kong.

Key Areas of Responsibilities

  • Conduct in-depth and insightful analysis of FX and interest rate markets in Asia, embedding the core global context while utilizing your deep understanding of the regulatory landscape, policy architecture, and market instruments in Asia.

  • Generate investment and hedging recommendations for clients based on analysis of macroeconomic, economic policies, and market dynamics.

  • Collaborate with internal economics team members to get their economic insights to be used for trading strategies and provide insights to clients.

  • Produce well-researched reports and contribute to regional/global publications, focusing on investment opportunities and trading recommendations across Asian FX/rates markets.

  • Present your ideas and recommendations to internal and external clients, including through marketing trips to different regions.

Requirements

  • Master’s degree or above in an economics (and/or finance) discipline.

  • Minimum 10+ years of relevant experience as a Strategist covering FX and Rates products, with a proven track record.

  • In-depth understanding of Asian economies and markets, encompassing regulatory landscape, policy architecture, and market instruments.

  • Strong interpersonal skills, enabling effective collaboration with internal teams and clients.

  • Excellent problem solving and analytical skills, creative thinker, and a keen ability to curate investment relevant analysis.

  • An individual with a proactive mindset, takes initiative, express intellectual curiosity, propose new ideas, deliver on independent projects, and excel in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong quantitative skills are an advantage, including economic/market modelling, econometric analysis, and coding. Strong Excel skills are a must.

  • Fluent in both spoken and written English, ideally Mandarin as well.

  • Stay up to date on regulatory requirements, ensure compliance with relevant regulations and maintain relevant licenses.

jobs.title: Quantitative Credit Strategist
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Job Title Quantitative Credit Strategist

Location London

Corporate Title Associate

Group Strategic Analytics (GSA) is part of Group Chief Operation Office (COO) which acts as the bridge between the Bank’s businesses and infrastructure functions to help deliver the efficiency, control, and transformation goals of the Bank.

You will join the quantitative credit strategists team working alongside Deutsche Bank’s European Flow Credit and Emerging Markets business. Our credit trading businesses are fully committed to technology as a key differentiator of performance and the partnership with quant strategists is seen as crucial to the future success of the desk. You will be a member of a small agile team based in London delivering risk, profit and loss (P&L) and pre-trade flow and relative value analytics solutions to bond trading and sales. You will be a highly motivated self-starter with a working understanding of credit markets and the associated credit modelling mathematics as well as being able to build production quality software applications and reports to tight timescales using appropriate technologies (KDB+/Q, Python, C++, Javascript). The position is full time on the trading floor in London and requires rapidly reacting to trader/sales/management demands in traditional ways but also using techniques in natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) to maximize our return on the large-scale data sets we curate.

What we’ll offer you

A healthy, engaged and well-supported workforce are better equipped to do their best work and, more importantly, enjoy their lives inside and outside the workplace. That’s why we are committed to providing an environment with your development and wellbeing at its centre.

You can expect:  

  • Competitive salary and non-contributory pension
  • 30 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, with the option to purchase additional days
  • Life Assurance and Private Healthcare for you and your family
  • A range of flexible benefits including Retail Discounts, a Bike4Work scheme and Gym benefits
  • The opportunity to support a wide ranging CSR programme + 2 days’ volunteering leave per year

Your key responsibilities

  • Development and support of daily flow analytics/risk/p&L systems
  • Actively collaborate in system architecture and design, ensuring a clear understanding of how components at all levels interact across the overall system
  • Discussing problems with the trading desk and gathering requirements for potential solutions.
  • Implementing flow analysis Management Information Systems (MIS) and reporting (e.g. volumes, market shares, hit rates, client profitability analysis)
  • Development of pre-trade analytics to support trading decisions (computing trade relative value metrics and strategy back testing)
  • Modelling expertise for a variety of quantitative problems the business has (e.g. portfolio optimization, flow matching, trade prospect ranking)

Your skills and experience

  • 3+ years front office investment banking experience in technical or quant roles
  • Highly proficient with programming in one or more of KDB+/Q, Python, C++, Javascript with experience in working with Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) tools in a collaborative environment (git/bitbucket/JIRA etc.)
  • Advanced Degree (PhD OR Masters) in a relevant subject such as Mathematics/Natural Science/Computer Science/Engineering
  • Experience working with data, both in onboarding, cleaning and curating data in databases as well as analysis and presentation
  • Experience in web development using JavaScript, Python, HTML5 with good analytical and quantitative skills. Experience of machine learning and natural language processing is desirable
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate and partner with various teams, and to be able to explain complex concepts effectively 

How we’ll support you

  • Coaching and support from experts in your team
  • A culture of continuous learning to aid progression
  • A range of flexible benefits that you can tailor to suit your needs
  • We value diversity and as an equal opportunities’ employer, we make reasonable adjustments for those with a disability such as the provision of assistive equipment if required (e.g. screen readers, assistive hearing devices, adapted keyboards)

About us

Deutsche Bank is the leading German bank with strong European roots and a global network. Click here to see what we do.

Deutsche Bank in the UK is proud to have been named The Times Top 50 Employers for Gender Equality 2025 for six consecutive years. Additionally, we have been awarded a Gold Award from Stonewall and named in their Top 100 Employers 2024 for our work supporting LGBTQ+ inclusion.

If you have a disability, health condition, or require any adjustments during the application process, we encourage you to contact our Adjustments Concierge adjustmentsconcierge@db.com to discuss how we can best support you. Alternatively, you can share your phone number, and a member of the team will be happy to call you to talk through your specific requirements.

We strive for a culture in which we are empowered to excel together every day. This includes acting responsibly, thinking commercially, taking initiative and working collaboratively.

Together we share and celebrate the successes of our people. Together we are Deutsche Bank Group.

We welcome applications from all people and promote a positive, fair and inclusive work environment.

jobs.title: Associate, Focus Investment Partners
jobs.description:
Associate, Focus Investment Partners

Boston, MA / New York, NY (Hybrid)

Position Summary:

The Associate, Focus Investment Partners will support the firm’s private equity and venture capital fundraising platform through a combination of operational execution, investor servicing, administrative coordination, and project management responsibilities. Working closely with senior team members, this individual will help drive the day-to-day execution behind fundraising processes, investor communications, reporting, onboarding, and relationship management activities while gaining exposure to private markets and institutional fundraising.

This role is ideal for an early-career professional with experience or interest in investment operations, private funds, investor relations, or fundraising support who is highly organized, detail-oriented, self-sufficient, and eager to learn. The position requires someone who can quickly absorb internal processes, proactively ask questions, and ultimately take ownership of recurring workflows and operational responsibilities with minimal oversight.

The near-term focus of the role is execution-heavy operational support across fundraising and investor servicing activities, with longer-term growth opportunities into investor relations, diligence support, fundraising strategy, and business development.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Provide operational and administrative support for the firm’s private equity and venture capital fundraising platform.
  • Help drive execution and coordination across fundraising processes, ensuring documents, trackers, follow-ups, approvals, and deliverables move forward accurately and on schedule.
  • Coordinate investor meetings, conference participation, fundraising events, and internal team activities.
  • Prepare meeting materials, fundraising presentations, investor communications, reporting packages, and organizational materials for internal and external use.
  • Manage investor records, CRM updates, fundraising pipelines, relationship management documentation, and internal tracking systems.
  • Assist with investor onboarding, subscription documentation, close trackers, due diligence requests, data room access, and ongoing investor information requests.
  • Coordinate and follow up with third-party administrators, custodians, platforms, and service providers (including CAIS, Ultimus, and similar partners) to support fundraising and onboarding workflows.
  • Serve as a point person for existing client relationships by responding to inquiries, coordinating follow-ups, resolving operational issues, and ensuring a high level of responsiveness and service.
  • Track fundraising activity, investor engagement, outstanding action items, and key business development initiatives across the platform.
  • Support senior team members by coordinating follow-up actions, maintaining project timelines, and ensuring operational workflows are executed efficiently and accurately.
  • Partner with internal teams across investments, operations, compliance, legal, and marketing to support fundraising, onboarding, and investor relations efforts.
  • Assist in developing and improving processes, reporting, organizational systems, and operational workflows to enhance team efficiency and scalability.
  • Conduct research and analysis on investors, market trends, fundraising opportunities, and industry developments as needed.
  • Support manager review and diligence processes by helping organize materials, summarize information, maintain diligence notes, and coordinate internal review workflows.
  • Participate in client and investor meetings to gain exposure to relationship management, fundraising activities, and private markets investing.
  • Take on increasing responsibility for investor communications, diligence coordination, relationship support, and fundraising initiatives as experience and knowledge develop.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, or a related field.
  • 0–2+ years of professional experience in investment operations, private funds, fund administration, asset management, wealth management, investor relations, or a related financial services environment.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with exceptional attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, workflows, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Self-sufficient, proactive, and comfortable taking ownership of recurring processes and operational responsibilities.
  • Quick learner with the ability to absorb new systems, workflows, and fundraising processes efficiently.
  • Demonstrated initiative, curiosity, and desire to learn the private markets and fundraising business.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
  • Experience working with CRM systems, investor databases, fundraising platforms, or operational tracking tools preferred.
  • Familiarity with private fund structures, subscription workflows, or investor onboarding processes is a plus.

This position is an exempt position. The annualized base pay range for this role is expected to be between [$85,000–$90,000] base salary compensation range. Actual base pay may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, experience, subject matter expertise, geographic location where work will be performed, and the applicant’s skill set. The base pay is just one component of the total compensation package. Other rewards may include an annual cash bonus and a comprehensive benefits package, including but not limited to medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and 401(k). Please note that the job title is subject to change based on the selected candidate’s experience and education.

About Focus Financial Partners

Focus is a leading financial services firm comprised of integrated wealth management, family office, and business management services. jobs.description:
This application form will be considered current for one year only. At the end of this period, if you are still interested in employment, it will be necessary for you to reapply by completing a new application form. All statements and questions are to be completed; the answers will be confidential.
Seaport Research Partners Overview
Seaport Research Partners (“SRP”) is a rapidly expanding, innovative research platform. SRP empowers self-driven analysts by reshaping economics and delivering a fully integrated solution to support, enhance and grow their franchise, allowing them to focus exclusively on producing the customized and differentiated research that matters most to clients. Seaport’s platform is increasingly attracting top analysts and buy-side customers alike.
Eighteen analysts have joined the platform since 2020 and bring an average of 20 years’ experience, most with prior experience at bulge bracket firms and many receiving industry recognition such as II rankings. SRP will continue to build upon this momentum by adding new analysts and verticals to its already broad coverage that currently includes Consumer, Energy, Financials, Industrials, Materials, SPAC’s, Utilities & Power sectors.
SRP operates as a division of Seaport Global Securities, which brings established global client relationships, access to over 3,000 opened institutional accounts, 150 senior salespeople & traders across the cap structure, asset management, global equity and debt capital markets, a full suite of corporate access services including multi-sector and niche conferences, fixed income & derivatives research and investment banking. Seaport Global’s offices throughout the US as well as London provide a superior network and deep infrastructure.
Opportunity
We are looking for experienced Equity Research Analysts who have an established franchise to join our expanding team. We have a strong presence in New York and Chicago, but have multiple offices across the US and Europe. We are flexible with location.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of 7 years’ experience within Equity Research.
  • Research coverage in sectors that complement our existing coverage.
  • Strong buy-side client relationships with a track record of driving revenues.
  • Strong corporate relationships with a track record of providing management access opportunities.
  • Idea generation and thought leadership abilities are essential.
  • Differentiated and proactive research with consistency and strong stock picking track record.
  • Ability to work in a team environment with sales, client service, trading, and capital markets teams.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a commitment to excellence and contributing to the team’s success.
  • Strong work ethic that prioritizes compliance and client service.
  • Strong communication, writing, and presentation skills.
  • MBA and/or CFA preferred.
  • Series 7 (or SIE), 63, 86, 87 license.

jobs.title: Senior Associate, Strategic Partnerships & Corporate Development
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

For over forty years, HarbourVest has been home to a committed team of professionals with an entrepreneurial spirit and a desire to deliver impactful solutions to our clients and investing partners. As our global firm grows, we continue to add individuals who seek a collaborative, open-door culture that values diversity and innovative thinking.

In our collegial environment that’s marked by low turnover and high energy, you’ll be inspired to grow and thrive. Here, you will be encouraged to build on your strengths and acquire new skills and experiences.

We are committed to fostering an environment of inclusion that promotes mutual respect among all employees. Understanding and valuing these differences optimizes the potential of both the individual and the firm.

HarbourVest is an equal opportunity employer.

This position will be a hybrid work arrangement. You will receive 18 remote workdays per quarter to use at your discretion, subject to manager approval. For example, you may choose to work in the office 4 days per week and take one remote day weekly (typically 13 weeks per quarter), leaving 5 additional remote days to be used as needed.

The Senior Associate, Strategic Partnerships and Corporate Development will work directly with senior partnership leaders to source, evaluate, structure, and carry out high-impact partnerships that broaden HarbourVest's distribution reach and product platform. The role covers distribution alliances with wealth platforms and intermediaries, strategic product collaborations, and other transactions that advance the firm's growth agenda.

This position is ideal for a current or former investment banking analyst or associate, or a similar corporate development, transaction advisory, or buy-side professional. The role offers the chance to apply transaction skills within a top private markets platform. It includes direct interaction with senior leaders and significant responsibility for complex deals from origination through closing.

Key Responsibilities:

Deal Execution

  • Own workstreams across partnership opportunities, from initial sizing and commercial diligence through negotiation, structuring, and onboarding
  • Build financial models, returns analyses, and economic sensitivities to evaluate proposed partnership structures
  • Prepare executive memos and decision-grade materials for senior leadership and the firm's investment and partnership committees
  • Partner with Legal on term sheet and definitive agreement negotiation

Strategic Analysis

  • Develop investment theses on prospective partners, distribution channels, and product opportunities
  • Benchmark competitor activity, industry trends, and emerging partnership models across the alternatives landscape
  • Convert market insights into actionable recommendations for senior leadership

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Drive cross-functional working groups across Product, Marketing, Sales, Legal, Client Operations, and Investor Relations to move opportunities to close

jobs.description:
Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Business - Infrastructure

Brookfield Infrastructure Group is one of Brookfield’s primary operating groups. The Infrastructure Group is one of the world’s largest infrastructure investors, owning and operating critical assets across the transport, utilities, energy, and data infrastructure sectors. The Group operates and manages approximately $191 billion of assets owned through its private funds and publicly listed entity, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners. Our portfolio of assets facilitate the movement and storage of energy, water, freight, passengers and data, and are located in North and South America, Europe and the Asia Pacific regions. For more information, visit: https://www.brookfield.com/our-businesses/infrastructure

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture.  We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader:  Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined.  Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.


Job Description

Brookfield Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Fund

Brookfield Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Fund (“BAIIF” or “the Fund”) is Brookfield’s inaugural strategy dedicated to investing in the physical infrastructure underpinning artificial intelligence. The Fund targets opportunities across the full AI value chain—including digital hubs and AI factories, compute hardware, power transmission, and strategic adjacencies—positioning Brookfield to capitalize on the transformative growth of AI technologies.

The Fund builds on Brookfield’s leadership in infrastructure and deep operating capabilities to scale critical AI subsectors (data centers, power and wireless infrastructure) to capitalize on the over $7-trillion opportunity of investment in physical infrastructure required to support the $10-trillion potential productivity gain from AI adoption.

The Fund, with a once in a generational opportunity to build the backbone of AI, has initially been built out by a dedicated team drawn from Brookfield’s infrastructure group, including senior executives with experience in recent data center acquisitions.

Key strategic principles include:

  • Focus on high-quality real assets or highly contracted businesses that underpin AI. 
  • Leverage Brookfield’s global operating presence and local relationships to access niche opportunities.
  • Utilize existing capabilities in data infrastructure and power development to scale AI infrastructure platforms.

Position Summary

This position offers a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing team focused on deploying capital across the AI infrastructure value chain.

Successful candidates will contribute to deal execution, due diligence, and asset management, working closely with senior leaders to scale Brookfield’s presence in this transformative sector. While primarily aligned with BAIIF, this role may also support adjacent strategies across Brookfield’s infrastructure and transition platforms.

Responsibilities

Investment Analysis & Execution

  • Develop and oversee detailed financial models and return analyses to evaluate potential investments across AI infrastructure sectors (e.g., data centers, compute hardware, power, and connectivity).
  • Lead or support due diligence processes, including financial, operational, legal, and tax workstreams, ensuring alignment with the investment thesis and business case.
  • Prepare and present investment committee materials, bid letters, and transaction documentation with increasing ownership at senior levels.

Deal Origination & Strategy

  • Source and evaluate new investment opportunities, leveraging industry research and market intelligence.
  • Contribute to or lead idea generation for transactions and deal structures, including identifying value creation strategies and market entry points.
  • Assist in implementing business development and transaction strategies, including networking and relationship-building to uncover new opportunities.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with operating teams across Brookfield’s infrastructure and transition platforms to support due diligence and post-investment asset management.
  • Coordinate with internal legal, tax, and structuring teams to ensure transaction execution aligns with strategic and financial objectives.

Leadership & Culture

  • Foster a collaborative, dynamic, and team-oriented culture that supports personal development, mentorshipskill-building—especially for junior colleagues.
  • Lead or contribute to special projects and ad hoc initiatives that advance fund strategy or operational excellence.

Market Research & Thought Leadership

  • Conduct deep industry and market research to inform investment strategies and identify emerging trends in AI infrastructure.
  • Help establish and refine investment theses, including competitive positioning and long-term growth drivers.

Key Qualifications

  • Exceptional analytical skills with deep expertise in financial and investment analysis, including advanced financial modelling capabilities.
  • Highly self-motivated and adaptable, with a proven ability to thrive in fast-paced environments, manage shifting priorities, and consistently meet deadlines.
  • Professional and collaborative, with a strong ability to contribute meaningfully within dynamic, team-oriented settings.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a track record of engaging effectively across all levels of an organization.
  • Meticulous attention to detail, combined with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams in performance-driven environments.
  • Strong interest in AI investment strategies.
  • Relevant sector experience in AI, infrastructure, and general private equity considered an asset.

Other Requirements

  • A professional, positive attitude and capable of contributing to a dynamic and team-oriented culture;
  • Experience in investment banking, restructuring, TMT and/or infrastructure investments or other relevant areas;
  • High level of proficiency in Excel and Power Point and very strong financial modelling skills.

Brookfield is committed to maintaining a Positive Work Environment that is safe and respectful; our shared success depends on it.  Accordingly, we do not tolerate workplace discrimination, violence or harassment.

Brookfield is committed to creating an accessible and inclusive organization. We are committed to providing barrier-free and accessible employment practices in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. Should you require a Human Rights Code-protected accommodation through any stage of the recruitment process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Our team of senior professionals delivers a wide array of strategic advisory, shareholder advisory, restructuring and special situations and private fund advisory and placement services to corporations, financial sponsors, institutional investors and governments around the world. We offer a unique portfolio of advisory services designed to help our clients achieve their strategic objectives. We also provide, through PJT Park Hill, private fund advisory and fundraising services for alternative investment managers, including private equity funds, real estate funds and hedge funds.

From the beginning, PJT Partners has firmly believed that having the best people is key to building an enduring franchise. Our perspective was, and remains, that a great team brings in both top tier clients and appeals to a wide-range of diverse, talented colleagues. Fostering an inclusive culture, which welcomes differing perspectives and beliefs, enables us to provide the best advice and insights to our clients.

To learn more about PJT Partners, please visit our website atwww.pjtpartners.com. 

Responsibilities:

PJT Park Hill (“Park Hill”) is our industry-leading advisor and intermediary business focused on alternative investment vehicles in the private equity, real estate, hedge fund and secondary advisory asset classes.

The Private Capital Solutions group, our secondary advisory practice, is one of the most experienced investment banking teams in the industry and has been involved in some of the largest, most complex transactions since the team’s founding in 2008. The practice leverages the firm’s global relationships to deliver superior results across the secondaries universe. Our highly specialized team focuses on delivering independent advisory and execution services to financial sponsors and institutional investors across a broad spectrum of strategic transactions including:

  • Financial Sponsor Solutions: Fund recapitalizations, continuation vehicles, fund restructurings, tender offers, preferred equity / other debt oriented solutions, management team spinouts and portfolio asset sales
  • Structured Liquidity Solutions: Securitizations, refinancings of illiquid financial holdings and joint ventures 
  • Institutional Investor Solutions: Divesture of private fund interests, valuation of private fund interests, transaction structuring and execution support.

Analysts within the Private Capital Solutions - Secondaries group work directly with clients in evaluating, structuring and recommending financial and strategic alternatives. The remit of the position spans the private capital spectrum with an emphasis on private equity secondary transactions. The role is industry and asset class agnostic, and the Analyst will be a generalist across transactions.

Analysts are key deal team members who are staffed directly on client teams and are expected to be involved in all aspects of a transaction, including due diligence, valuation analysis, client and process management, and investor engagement.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Researcher
jobs.description:
About the position

We’re looking for smart and curious individuals from industry and academia to join our growing team and drive our ML work.

On our Machine Learning team, you'll build the deep learning models that power our trading strategies, supported by our rapidly growing computing cluster with tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. Trading poses unusual challenges— large models and nonstationary datasets in a competitive multi-agent environment—that force us to search for novel techniques. 

Researchers, engineers and traders sit a few feet away from each other and work together to train models, architect systems and run trading strategies. Depending on the day, we might be diving deep into market data, tuning hyperparameters, debugging distributed training performance or studying how our model likes to trade in production.

We’ll rely on your in-depth knowledge of the machine learning landscape and understanding of a variety of approaches—drawn from LLMs, image models, RL agents, recommendation systems or classical ML methods—to shape the future of ML at Jane Street. You’ll train models for the next generation of our deep learning-based trading strategies, and build the fundamental understanding we need to tackle new markets and situations. You’ll also be hiring new colleagues, attending conferences and teaching techniques to teammates—all of which we consider to be real and impactful parts of the job.

About you

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. There’s no fixed set of skills we are looking for, but you should bring:

  • Practical experience working on empirical ML problems
  • The ability to apply logical and mathematical thinking to all kinds of problems
  • Intellectual curiosity and excitement about state-of-the-art research across many ML problem domains
  • Fluency with a versatile set of models and tricks 
  • The hands-on coding skills needed to rapidly implement and iterate on your ideas, in Python and your favourite ML framework
  • An eagerness to ask questions, admit mistakes  and learn new things
  • Fluency in English required

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

The Associate will be an integral part of the Corporate Development team. The primary mandate of the team is to partner with business leaders across the organization to evaluate and execute new business opportunities that support the long-term growth strategy of the firm, including supporting the incubation of new business lines, participating in the evaluation of strategic investments and partnerships, and execution of M&A opportunities as they pertain to the talent, assets, and/or corporate entities. The Associate is expected to work closely with Finance and FP&A to prepare analyses, financial models, investment memorandum, and presentation materials in support of corporate development efforts.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Evaluate and execute new business opportunities, including incubation of new products and services, strategic investments, and corporate acquisitions in the commercial real estate industry.
  • Conduct market research to identify potential new acquisitions.
  • Build financial valuation models and analysis of investment returns, including those are related to the acquisition of production talent.
  • Prepare investment memorandum and other supporting materials to communicate investment and capital allocation rationale to internal stakeholders.
  • Support corporate finance and investor relations efforts as it relates to the management of Lument Finance Trust (“LFT”), our publicly traded commercial mortgage REIT: Prepare and maintain quarterly presentation materials, including performance updates, portfolio analytics, and other ad hoc materials for the management team and independent board of directors.
  • Collaborate with Accounting to produce quarterly earnings supplemental presentations for LFT’s public stakeholders.
  • Provide management team with other analytical support and investor relations efforts as needed.
  • Maintain industry and competitor surveillance related to Lument’s competitive positioning.
  • Coordinate across functional groups to analyze internal data and assist with operational, strategic, and other analytical projects.
  • Other projects and duties as assigned  

Travel Requirements: <10%

Education, Skills and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related field
  • 2-5 years relevant work experience in the CRE finance, investment management, or commercial banking industries
  • Working knowledge of GAAP financial statements and an ability to build forecast models in Excel
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Powerpoint, Word, etc.)
  • Interest in commercial real estate finance and investment management
  • Creative and effective problem-solving skills, excellent organizational and analytical skills
  • The ability to work well under pressure, adjust to varied workloads and handle multiple priorities, with a sense of urgency
  • This position requires access to sensitive and confidential information. It is expected that this information remain both internally and external to the company as applicable. Candidate must demonstrate the ability to maintain confidentiality and to use discretion in the performance of daily activities
  • Excellent organizational, communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to plan, organize, and prioritize assignments, and to meet critical and established deadlines; Ability to manage multiple assignments ant transactions simultaneously
  • Ability to learn quickly and demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of a lean, high-performance team

Annual base salary gross: $110,000-$135,000 (NY only). The base salary range represents the estimated low and high end of ORIX’s salary for this position based on geography. Actual base salaries will vary and will be based on various factors, such as candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies and proficiency for the role. The base pay is one component of ORIX’s total compensation package for employees. Other rewards and benefits include cash bonuses, long term incentives, health insurance, accident and life insurance, and retirement benefits.  Please visit our Benefits page for additional information.

Life at ORIX

We are committed to the health and well-being of our employees and offer a quality, competitive benefits package that provides valuable healthcare and financial protection for our workforce, while emphasizing a healthy work/life balance.

You Time

We want you to have the time needed to recharge and manage life with our competitive vacation policy, floating personal holidays, extensive leave options, our annual observed holidays, and more.

Family Care

Every family has a different journey and ORIX USA Group is proud to offer extensive benefit programs such as: infertility coverage, adoption support, child and elder care, fully paid maternity, and generous parental leave benefits to help you and your families along the way.

Flexible Work Arrangements

ORIX associates enjoy the advantages of our hybrid working model with a 3 day in-office minimum requirement.

ORIX USA is an equal opportunity employer, providing equal employment opportunities (EEO), and is committed to diversifying its workforce. All employees and applicants for employment will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, protected veteran status or other status protected by law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment.

jobs.description:
About Invesco

As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

What’s in it for you?

Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including:

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Hybrid work schedule 

  • 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution 

  • Health & wellbeing benefits 

  • Parental Leave benefits 

  • Employee stock purchase plan

Job Description

The role:

The Thematic & Specialty ETF Strategist will leverage his/her capital markets, investment management and product knowledge to deliver macro views and product positioning to institutions and financial advisors. The role will work collaboratively with Product Development, Product Management, Portfolio Management, Capital Markets, Sales and Marketing to position and grow the product line.


Responsibilities of the role:

  • Drive growth of the thematic & specialty equity ETF product line in partnership with cross-functional teams (sales, marketing, capital markets, product management, portfolio management and product development)
  • Help build and reinforce a brand for Invesco ETF products by presenting at industry conferences and serving as the “voice” for the product line in media interviews, sponsored events, webcasts, etc.
  • Support efforts to develop and manage insights on the product line through asset class and product-specific communication ; product training and positioning ; product-specific competitive analysis ; market and product performance commentaries; and content development in partnership with Marketing
  • Partner with Sales to execute product-specific distribution strategies and participate in client meetings
  • Monitor macro market conditions to formulate asset class views, and translate them into actionable investment and product positioning ideas for clients
  • Identify new product opportunities as well as assess existing product line to identify opportunities for enhancement

Requirements of the role:

  • 10+ years of investment management or research experience, with strong understanding of equity markets.
  • ETF and/or index product knowledge and relevant industry experience required.
  • Excellent written communication, oral presentation, and analytical skills.
  • Proven ability to present effectively at corporate, client, and industry events, including large audiences.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative mindset; able to build effective relationships across all levels.
  • Self-directed professional who can set objectives and work independently while seeking guidance as needed.
  • Undergraduate degree in business, finance, or related field required; MBA, CFA, CIMA, or CFP preferred.

jobs.title: Senior Portfolio Accounting Analyst
jobs.description:
The Role

This is a full-time role based in Dallas, Texas. Sixth Street has an immediate opening for a bright, hard-working individual to join our Portfolio Accounting – Insurance team in Dallas. This team is focused on supporting accounting and reporting activities across our Insurance SMAs investing in private and liquid investments across various sectors (Asset Based Finance, Structured Credit, Infrastructure, Energy etc). The role will be an integral part of a developing team in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial work environment. This individual will be involved in several facets of the operations, including cash and investment position reconciliation, accounting activities, reporting and investment performance/analysis deliverables etc.

Core Responsibilities

  • Manage all accounting responsibilities and work with the Operations and Offshore accounting teams to support, record and reconcile investing and related cash activities
  • Review investment related documents and monitor new investment setup in the accounting platform
  • Liaison with investment professionals on structuring, cash movements and investment performance
  • Assist with preparing complex waterfall and management fee calculations in accordance with Investment Management Agreements (IMAs)
  • Assist with expense reporting and analysis
  • Assist with quarterly valuation process
  • Assist with the production of daily, monthly and quarterly reporting that is distributed to all Investors, Investment Professionals and Management.
  • Assist fundraising team in preparing marketing documents
  • Participate in a wide variety of special projects, both operating and financial, and compile a variety of special reports

What We Value

  • Strong written and oral communication skills
  • Strong understanding and application of accounting rules and industry accounting practices
  • Detail-oriented, responsible and proactive
  • Deadline-oriented to meet time-sensitive regulatory and contractual requirements
  • Adept at problem solving
  • Candidate must be self-motivated and willing to work in a team environment
  • Candidate must have attention to detail and be focused on multiple demands and deliverables

Preferred

  • 3-5 years accounting experience in a combination of public accounting (either audit or tax), alternative asset or investment management firm, or fund admin
  • Experience with alternative investments, credit and structured products investments, private equity and partnership accounting, fund administration, and Advent Geneva are preferred
  • Experience with investment performance reporting and analytics are a plus
  • Strong accounting and excel skills; professional certification (CPA or equivalent)

About Sixth Street

Founded in 2009, Sixth Street is a leading global investment firm dedicated to developing themes and offering solutions to companies across all stages of growth.

Our firm is designed for cross-platform collaboration at scale: we build businesses, invest for growth, acquire assets, provide direct financing, identify value in public markets, purchase royalty streams, and regularly develop first-of-their-kind structures to meet the strategic objectives of management teams.

We do all this globally and as one unified team of investment and control-side professionals working on behalf of our institutional investors and their beneficiaries around the world.

We believe adhering to our core values is a competitive advantage. Everyone on our team contributes their perspectives and expertise to help us solve complex challenges and get to the right answer. At Sixth Street, the best idea wins.

For more information, visit the Sixth Street Careers site or follow us .

Sixth Street is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, genetic history, marital status, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, veteran or military status, disability, genetic predisposition, status as a victim of domestic violence, a sex offense or stalking, or any other class or status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Sixth Street will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.   

If you need a reasonable accommodation to fill out this application, please contact Cindy Bombara (cbombara@sixthstreet.com). 

Please refer to the privacy notice on our website for additional information regarding our obligations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”).

If you are not eligible for this role, please refer to our Careers Page for other opportunities.

jobs.description:
ABOUT TERRACE GROUP HOLDINGS:

Terrace Group Holdings is a Los Angeles–based real estate development firm focused exclusively on ground-up Class A self-storage assets in California. The firm sources, entitles, and builds climate-controlled storage facilities across Southern California’s highest-barrier markets.

TGH currently has approximately $50 million of self-storage development under construction in Southern California, with a pipeline targeting $60 million or more of new development annually. The firm’s strategy combines disciplined site selection, deep municipal entitlement expertise, and hands-on development execution to deliver outsized risk-adjusted returns in a sector undergoing rapid institutional consolidation.

TGH is a lean, founder-led organization where every team member has a direct line to decision-making and a tangible impact on the trajectory of the business.

THE OPPORTUNITY:

Reporting to the Director of Acquisitions & Development (or Managing Partner), this position is responsible for managing the pre-development and entitlement process for self-storage development projects, including coordinating with government agencies, managing consultants and third-party vendors, securing permits, and overseeing project schedules and budgets through construction.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Schedule and lead preliminary meetings with government agencies, engineers, architects, and third-party consultants for new development projects.
  • Create and maintain schedules and deadlines for entitlement and permit timelines based on city and consultant feedback, with consistent updates to stakeholders.
  • Negotiate and execute development-related contracts.
  • Coordinate with various governmental entities throughout the entitlement and permitting process.
  • Coordinate attorneys, architects, and third-party consultants across active projects.
  • Create bidding packages for contractors.
  • Secure all building permits required for construction.
  • Oversee project budgets and manage project expenses in alignment with approved budgets.
  • Provide development and construction oversight across active projects.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Invoice processing and approval routing.
  • Document management and project-level filing.
  • Third-party follow-up and coordination on administrative matters.
  • Schedule management and timeline tracking.
  • Interact with accounting representatives on project-related expenses.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Oversight of Construction Manager’s day-to-day activities, deliverables, and reporting.
  • Oversight of contractors, subcontractors, and vendors related to project activities, invoices, and contract execution.

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:

  • BA/BS degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Urban Planning, or related field.
  • A minimum of five years of experience in real estate development and/or construction, with demonstrated knowledge of the entitlement, permitting, and construction process.
  • Experience with self-storage or industrial development preferred.
  • Familiarity with Southern California municipal entitlement and permitting processes preferred.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & ABILITIES:

  • Strong understanding of the real estate development lifecycle from land acquisition through construction completion.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Office, Microsoft Project, and project management software.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously across different stages of development.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordinating with government agencies, consultants, and internal stakeholders.
  • Detail-oriented with ability to manage schedules, budgets, and complex timelines.
  • Must be fluent in using AI tools and large language models (LLMs), with the ability to proactively apply them to research, analysis, drafting, and workflow efficiency.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

  • Competitive base salary and benefits commensurate with experience
  • This role is based in Los Angeles, CA and requires full-time, in-office presence
  • Actual base salary considers several factors including but not limited to geography, job-related knowledge, experience, and budget. The start of the salary range is typically associated with the minimum experience required. The anticipated base salary range for the position in Los Angeles, CA is $130,000 - $150,000.
  • #LI-KO1

About Invesco

As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

What’s in it for you?

Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including:

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Hybrid work schedule 

  • 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution

Job Description

About the Role:

Invesco is seeking a Senior Product Manager to support investment strategies within its Fundamental Equities franchise, as part of the Americas Product Management team. The platform manages $281B in assets with 110+ professionals delivering 70 equity strategies across 7 global locations to clients in 25+ countries. This role is responsible for overseeing product collateral, reporting, and strategic initiatives that support business development across retail, institutional, and retirement channels. The Senior Product Manager partners closely with CPMs, portfolio teams, and cross-functional stakeholders to align on product positioning, messaging, and commercial priorities while maintaining deep expertise in equity strategies and market trends. This individual will also lead and develop team members, drive enterprise-wide initiatives, and leverage strong analytical, communication, and relationship management skills to deliver impactful outcomes.

Responsibilities of the Role:

  • Lead month and quarter-end product collateral updates, producing and maintaining presentations, factsheets, commentaries, infographics, annual reports, and risk/performance attribution reporting
  • Partner cross-functionally (legal, compliance, risk, technology, sales, and marketing) to deliver accurate, compliant, and timely product messaging aligned with firm standards
  • Support regulatory and governance requirements, including fund board materials, prospectus/SAI reviews, and related reporting deliverables
  • Serve as a key partner to marketing and RFP teams by managing product data integrity, consultant databases, and RFP/DDQ content and positioning
  • Ensure quality control across websites and internal platforms, maintaining current, accurate, and compliant product content
  • Drive product change management by coordinating stakeholders and ensuring timely updates across collateral systems and client communications
  • Partner closely with CPMs and investment teams to build deep expertise, align on strategy positioning, and support marketing materials, client communications, and sales enablement
  • Lead as a player/coach by supporting key strategies directly while managing and mentoring product team members, delegating workflows, and upholding quality and performance standards

Requirements for the role:

  • 5–7 years of experience in financial services, preferably within asset management; bachelor’s degree required (business or related field preferred)  
  • Strong understanding of equities, financial markets, and core investment concepts and processes
  • Experience leading and developing others in a player/coach capacity
  • Advanced technical proficiency across Microsoft Office, Morningstar, eVestment, Bloomberg, and related tools; familiarity with AI tools preferred
  • Strong analytical capabilities with experience in data and content management, research, writing, and marketing support
  • Passion for capital markets and the investment management industry
  • Entrepreneurial, change-oriented mindset with a focus on innovation, continuous improvement, and creative problem solving
  • Excellent communication skills, strong attention to detail and deadlines, sound judgment, and drive to succeed; Series 7 & 63 required within 6 months of hire

jobs.description:
About the program

At Jane Street, our internships center around hands-on mentorship and a robust educational curriculum that includes challenging classes, interactive sessions, and small group discussions. Over the course of 10-12 weeks, you’ll be matched with full-time employees who will mentor you as you tackle real-world projects. 

You’ll also have time to use our office amenities, attend guest speakers and social events, and get a real sense of what it would be like to work here full time.

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company—many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind, a collaborative nature, and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in.

About the position

Our goal is to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. As an intern, you'll be paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on real-world projects we actually need done.

As an SP Intern, you'll work on projects that combine big-picture thinking with rigorous analytical problem-solving. You'll learn to break down complex challenges into actionable steps, use data to inform decisions, and build frameworks to tackle business questions. This hands-on experience will give you direct insight into how SPs lead strategic initiatives across the organization and leave you with a strong grasp of what an SP career looks like.

If you'd like to learn more, you can explore our Strategy and Product program and interview process. You can also learn more about Jane Street's internship program here.

About you

If you've never thought about a career in finance, you're in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind, a collaborative nature, and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you'll fit right in. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

  • Someone who excels at taking a structured and careful approach to solving problems, communicates effectively, can drive projects forward, and has exceptional attention to detail
  • Excited to learn about a wide range of disciplines and subject matter, including global market dynamics, technical systems and tooling, operational infrastructure, and more
  • Eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and constantly deepen your understanding
  • Available to start working full-time in September 2028

We review applications on a rolling basis and treat all applications equally, regardless of when you apply. While we plan on staying open through the fall, we encourage you to apply by September 30th to help you plan around any other recruiting processes you're going through.

jobs.title: IGPC Deal Lead
jobs.description:
About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About the Role

As part of the continued expansion of our Private Investing capabilities, we are seeking to recruit a Deal Lead to join our Investment Grade Private Credit (IGPC) team. Wellington has been investing in private markets since 2003, and the Firm launched its first dedicated private capital fund in 2014. Today, the private investment teams manage approximately $11 billion in assets in aggregate across private growth equity, venture capital and private credit, and it is the fastest growing investment group within Wellington. 

The Deal Lead will work closely with the senior investment team across all aspects of the deal process, including originating, underwriting, structuring, executing, and monitoring globally sourced privately placed debt securities, with a focus on structured and asset-backed transactions. This individual will leverage an established network across banks, sponsors, advisors, and issuers to drive differentiated deal flow. The role requires demonstrated experience executing complex structured and asset-backed private placements, including collateral analysis, structural review, cash flow modeling, and legal documentation assessment. The Deal Lead will originate and evaluate investment opportunities, conduct in-depth due diligence, develop investment recommendations, and oversee credits through their lifecycle. Responsibilities include ongoing portfolio monitoring, assessment of structural performance and covenant compliance, and support of strategic investment decisions in partnership with investment and legal teams.


ESSENTIAL SKILLS
The following essential skills are required for the role:

  • Analytical acumen, modeling, research, and passion – The ideal candidate will have strong financial modeling and analytical skills, and the ability to synthesize complex information into clear, well-supported investment recommendations. The ability to synthesize disparate information, identify the most important elements, and arrive at a conclusion is required. In addition, the Deal Lead will emphasize fundamental/thematic, research-driven approach to underwriting asset-backed structures and the ability to implement those ideas through a highly analytical and detailed approach. The successful candidate would have exposure to portfolio management, amendments and potential restructurings as well.

  • Superior collaboration and influencing skills – The Deal Lead will be a self-directed, hard-working team player, who contributes to the investment efforts of the IGPC team. The successful candidate will build strong relationships with issuers, industry contacts, financing partners, clients and prospects, as well as internally with colleagues on the investment and legal teams. The ability to take risks and challenge investment views is critical, as is the humility to admit mistakes and a desire to learn from others. The Deal Lead must recognize the benefits of diverse perspectives.  The ability to communicate (both verbally and in writing) and contribute to an open investment dialogue is required.

  • Intellectual curiosity, capacity for differentiated thinking, and a growth mindset – The flexibility and openness to continue learning, evolving, and growing as a Deal Lead is important.  The Deal Lead will have a global perspective and creative approach for analyzing private placement transactions.  Success in this role will open progression opportunities within the IGPC team and broader Wellington.

OTHER QUALIFICATIONS 
Additional qualifications and individual characteristics are likely to include:

  • A minimum of 7 years of relevant buy- or sell-side experience in structured finance private debt or credit research, with a focus on structured and asset-backed securities. 

  • Strong academic credentials: an undergraduate degree in finance, economics or accounting is preferred; 

  • Strong bottom-up fundamental approach to research; 

  • Demonstrated expertise in utilizing AI tools to accelerate market, industry, and issuer research, summarize large data sets, and identify patterns that enhance underwriting and monitoring workflows; 

  • Established network in the private debt and structured credit ecosystem including issuers, industry peers, and financing partners; 

  • Track record of developing, negotiating, and monitoring bespoke covenants; 

  • Strong work ethic and attention to detail; 

  • Ability to organize, manage, and prioritize time well;

  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and make decisions in the face of uncertainty;

  • Independence of thought, an entrepreneurial nature, and a global perspective;

  • Sound judgment, strong work ethic and highest personal and professional integrity; and

  • Willingness to travel. 

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications?  That’s ok. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply and welcome a chance to review your background. We are dedicated to building and maintaining a diversified workforce and considering a broad array of candidates with a variety of skill, workplace experiences, and backgrounds.

As an equal opportunity employer, Wellington Management ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, creed, national origin, age, ancestry, disability (physical or mental), medical condition, citizenship, marital status, pregnancy, veteran or military status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you are a candidate with a disability, or are assisting a candidate with a disability, and require an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please email us at GMWTalentOperations@wellington.com.

At Wellington Management, our approach to compensation is designed to help us attract, inspire and retain the best talent in our industry. We strive to pay employees fairly and competitively across all levels and roles. Our approach to compensation considers all aspects of total compensation; all employees are eligible to receive salary, variable compensation, and benefits. The base salary range for this position is:

USD 120,000 - 225,000

This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered when making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; role; skills and experience; certifications; and education. This range is an estimate, and further details on salary and total compensation aspects will be shared with candidates during the recruitment process.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering or another quantitative subject

  • Minimum two years of relevant experience, working hands on with quantitative tools demonstrating data analysis skills; Preferably experience gained in financial markets and equities market microstructure

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

  • Proficient in Python and programming skills
